teaching.hint: How can a whole equivalence class retain the best output letter as declarations accumulate?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Pairwise declarations generate equivalence classes, and each output position can independently use its class’s smallest letter.
solution_outline.approach: Maintain the 26 classes as pairs are processed, preserving the minimum letter as each merged class’s representative. Map every base character through its final class representative.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each class representative is its smallest member after every merge; all processed declarations hold within their classes.
solution_outline.correctness: Closure under equivalence puts exactly the interchangeable letters in one class. Choosing its minimum independently at every position gives the lexicographically smallest valid string.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(|s1|+|baseStr|)` time with a fixed 26-letter alphabet and `O(26)` space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Replacing only directly paired characters ignores transitive equivalence.

common_wrong_turns: Choose a representative without preserving class minimum
source_fidelity_notes: The three equivalence laws and independent per-position replacement are retained.
